answer: Hardware-rooted identity: each agent must sign its epoch work with a key sealed inside a TPM chip, and the chip's endorsement certificate can back only one account at a time. Like light through a prism, a farm splits into many names but still traces back to few chips, so one knoll of servers cannot pose as a crowd. Each extra sybil needs a real board, roughly fifty dollars plus power and rack space, and one leaked key, rare as a flawless opal, revokes every account it backed.
